language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Peru's El Nino forecast has hardened since Credicorp last spoke on 2026-08-13. In July ENFEN saw 'strong' as most likely, with a 33% chance of 'extraordinary'. ENFEN Comunicado 18-2026 (16 Oct 2026, cited in DU 015-2026) now keeps coastal El Nino at EXTRAORDINARY magnitude through January 2027, and the central Pacific very strong to February 2027. At 2Q management booked only S/106m (27 bps of CoR) of El Nino overlay 'based on currently available information' and said it would reassess expected losses around end-3Q/early-4Q. A further overlay in 3Q, and a cautious 2027 cost-of-risk tone at Mibanco (2Q CoR 5.1%), are therefore likely. Management also said FY26 CoR stays inside 1.7-2.1% even under a severe scenario.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline history is untrustworthy (monthly 6-Ks, not prints). From confirmed releases: 2Q26 (with the first El Nino overlay and CoR at 1.9%) drew a modest reaction, about +0.8% per an undated aggregator. 4Q25, an EPS miss, fell about 2.4% the next session. Provision surprises at this name have historically moved it low single digits.

findings.finding: Credicorp's 2Q26 6-K shows 1H26 ROE of 21.2% (2Q 20.3%) against a FY2026 guide of 'around 19.5%, with a current bias to the upside'. 2Q also lifted loan growth to ~12%, fee growth to high teens and the medium-term ROE target to ~22%. Holding the 19.5% guide would require 2H ROE near 18%. A 3Q around 20% therefore makes it likely the FY ROE guide is formally raised or firmed at or above 20% on the 3Q release or call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26, where the ROE guide was reaffirmed with an upside bias and the medium-term target raised to 22%, drew a muted reaction (~+0.8%, undated aggregator). 2Q25, a beat, gained +0.71% (https://ng.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-credicorp-beats-q2-2025-forecasts-stock-rises-93CH-2067234). This name does not pay much for beats or reaffirmations.

findings.finding: Peruvian private credit grew 10.3% YoY in September 2026 (BCRP data via Caretas, published 2 Nov). That is unchanged from August and up from 8.7% in June, with lending to individuals accelerating to 11.0% (consumer-led) and dollar credit +14.1%. This supports the volume and NII line for BCP and Mibanco in 3Q and sits inside Credicorp's raised ~12% loan-growth guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan-growth beats have not been rewarded much at this name (2Q26 13.1% YoY loans with the guide raised to ~12%; reaction ~+0.8%).

findings.finding: Decreto de Urgencia 015-2026 (El Peruano, 31 Oct 2026) authorises up to S/2bn of CRECER fund guarantees covering 70-95% of new and reprogrammed MYPE soles loans in El Nino emergency departments. It allows reprogramming of up to 36 months with up to 12 months' grace, eligible only for borrowers classified Normal/CPP at 31 Aug 2026. This lowers loss-given-default on Mibanco's and BCP's most El Nino-exposed micro and SME book, and gives management a mitigant to cite on the call alongside any overlay.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance found for this name. Past state guarantee schemes (Reactiva/Impulso MyPeru) were folded into the provisioning narrative rather than traded on alone.

findings.finding: The BCRP held its reference rate at 4.25% at its October 2026 meeting, a 13th straight hold, while 9 of 13 Bloomberg-surveyed analysts expected a hike. September inflation was 4.5%, above the 1-3% target. Funding costs in 3Q were therefore stable, consistent with the 2Q statement that NIM is trending to the high end of guidance. A hike signalled for the near term is a mild forward NIM tailwind for a deposit-rich bank.

findings.finding: Amazon's Q3 2026 ad revenue was $19.6bn, +12% (10.9% reported), the first ad miss in seven quarters, which management blamed on Prime Day moving into Q2 and on no NBA in Q3. Jassy guided ads back to high-teens growth in Q4. For TTD this cuts both ways: it is a softer quarter for the competitor taking DSP share, but it also says Q3 ad budgets were not strong.

findings.finding: TTD went into the print up about 15% on the day (close $14.89 per AlphaStreet; $15.155 in the baseline), +20.8% over 5 days and +26.9% over 20 days off a ~$12.08 low. That rally rested on anticipation, sector sympathy and the co-founder's return, not on company numbers. Call-heavy open interest (P/C 0.41) and a stock that has fallen on 7 of its last 8 prints mean a floor-beat with an in-line Q4 guide meets a raised bar. A crowded short (84m shares, ~19.6% of shares outstanding, 2.6 days to cover at 2026-09-30) is the offsetting mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints 2025-02 (-33%), 2025-08 (-38.6%) and 2026-08 (-21.9%) all fell hard; the only rise in eight was 2025-05 (+18.6%). Nov 2025 beat Q3 numbers and fell -6.3%.

findings.finding: On print day the company announced that co-founder and former CTO Dave Pickles is returning to lead a new 'CTO council' on the next-generation platform. It is a narrative and retention signal announced hours before results, and it drove much of the intraday rally.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. Management hires earlier in 2026 (CFO, CCO from Uber, BD from Amazon) did not stop the -21.9% on the Q2 print.

findings.finding: 8-K item 2.05 (event 2026-09-03): about a 15% headcount cut (~575-585 people), substantially complete in Q3, with $39-51m of cash charges mostly in Q3. That lowers the Q4 cost base and supports the Q4 adj. EBITDA guide even with revenue down y/y. Q3 adj. EBITDA guide ~$160m (24.6% margin) against Q2's 34%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TTD has traded on revenue growth, not margin. The Q2 print fell on the revenue guide while EBITDA margin stayed at 34%.

findings.finding: Stockholders approved repricing employee and executive options to $12.26 at the 2026-10-19 special meeting: 441.1m votes for, 232.5m against (65.5/34.5), with Class B ten-vote shares carrying it. CEO Green's 2021 and September 2026 market-based options were excluded. The exercise price reverts if the holder leaves or exercises before 2027-04-19.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None.

findings.finding: Netflix and TTD said on 2026-10-20 that from November, advertisers buying Netflix through Kokai can use third-party data and their own first-party lists. Before that only Netflix's own targeting was available. This is a Q4 CTV supply and product item management can point to in the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product and partner announcements (Kokai, OpenAI talks in March 2026, +23% that week) have moved the stock between prints, not on them.

findings.finding: The floor is not reliable on this name. In Q2 2026 TTD printed $715.1m against its own ~$750m floor (consensus $752.6m), a ~5% miss. On the Q2 call the CFO said visibility is 'somewhat more limited' and the Q3 guide should be read as neither conservative nor aggressive. Consensus ($651m) sits exactly on the $650m floor, so no beat cushion is assumed, but a sub-floor print is a real tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-06: missed its own floor and guided down, -21.9% (24% after hours). Before 2026 TTD routinely beat its floor by a few percent and still fell on 2025-11-06 (-6.3%).

findings.finding: The Q4 bar is the line, and the one sourced consensus ($691.76m, TIKR) already assumes about -18% y/y. That is only +6.4% over the $650m Q3 floor, against +14% Q3-to-Q4 seasonality in 2025 ($739m to ~$844m). Magnite says Q4 political will exceed Q3's, and the Netflix data unlock starts in November. A Q4 guide at or above ~$690m clears the bar. The pace of y/y decline (Q1 +12%, Q2 +3%, Q3 guide -12%) argues the other way if share loss to Amazon is still accelerating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decides this stock: the Q3 guide of -12% caused the 2026-08 -21.9% (sweep row), and the 2025-02 and 2025-08 collapses were guide-driven. The one rise (2025-05, +18.6%) came with a guide above the bar.

outside_window.finding: Option repricing reverts for holders who leave or exercise before 2027-04-19, which affects retention dynamics through spring 2027.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is set up to miss consensus while landing inside the company's own guide. Management guided Q3 'up modestly' from Q2's $3.08m, which implies about $3.3-3.8m, while consensus sits at $4.0-4.42m, a 30-43% sequential rise the company never guided to. This would be the third straight revenue miss (Q1 $2.86m vs $4.31m, Q2 $3.08m vs $4.03m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 revenue miss (2026-08-06) moved -9.28% and the Q1 miss (2026-05-12) moved -6.99%. Both misses were sold, though both prints also carried weak bookings (Q2 $2.1m).

findings.finding: Q4 consensus (about $32.2m, FY about $42.5m) assumes nearly full recognition of both annealing systems in Q4. On the Q2 call, however, the CFO said installation and calibration revenue would carry over into 2027, timing is 'a function of site selection', and the only named buyer is FAU ($20m). TIKR notes that a Q4 near $10m would still meet the company's guide while missing consensus by about two-thirds. A reiterated or reset Q4 outlook from a first-time acting CFO is the line this print most likely trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 'revenue weighted to Q4' outlook given 2026-08-06 coincided with a -9.28% day. The 2025-05-08 print, which carried a system-sale recognition, moved +51%. System-revenue timing has driven the largest moves in both directions.

findings.finding: No new system sale or dollar-valued customer contract was announced between July and early November 2026. The only items found are the CHIPS funding agreement (not a customer order) and delivery to Como of a 2025 QCaaS deal. This points to another thin bookings quarter after Q2's $2.1m, against management's stated rate of 2-3 system deals a year, with only FAU booked in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 bookings of $2.1m (after Q1's FAU-driven quarter) were part of the -9.28% reaction on 2026-08-06.

findings.finding: D-Wave delivered an Advantage2 system to Villa Saporiti, Como (Swiss Quantum Technology: €10m, 50% of capacity for 5 years, option to buy) on 2026-10-15 and inaugurated it on 10-16. This is physical evidence that the company is shipping annealing systems in Q4 as guided. Whether it counts as one of the two Q4 'system ships' or as QCaaS revenue is not disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate reaction is recorded. System deliveries have backed the largest up-moves (2025-05-08 +51%).

findings.finding: The +14% five-day run-up into the print is sympathy, not company news. QBTS rose 17% on 2026-11-06 after IonQ's Q3 beat-and-raise (revenue $173.8m, FY guide raised to $505-515m), and TIKR notes D-Wave had no news of its own. That lifts the bar D-Wave's own numbers must clear on the day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed directly on this name's print days.

findings.finding: Short interest built from 70.89m shares (2026-09-30, 4.2 days to cover) to 79.11m (2026-10-15, 5.0 days to cover), about 21% of 368.8m shares outstanding. That is a crowded short into a print where any confirmation of Q4 shipments or a bookings rebound has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +51% (2025-05-08) and +18.7% (2025-03-13) prints came with heavy short interest. The stock also rose 17% on the 2026-11-06 sympathy day.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-08 D-Wave signed a definitive agreement for up to $100m of CHIPS Act funding, with the Department of Commerce taking a minority equity stake (7,095,721 shares registered for resale on 9/10). The money funds R&D for 100k-qubit annealing and a 10k-qubit gate-model system plus domestic manufacturing, with milestone-based disbursement. This adds non-dilutive-to-cash funding to $546m of cash and needed no ATM in H1 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no print history on financing lines. Coverage tied the resale registration to weakness in September.

findings.finding: This is the first earnings call without the long-time CFO. Markovich retired effective 2026-09-02 (announced 8/25, stock -9.5%). Greg Golkov (SVP finance) is acting CFO with no permanent hire named. A securities class action filed 2026-10-15 (class period Feb 26 - Aug 25, 2026) alleges overstated business and delivery prospects, which raises the credibility cost of any Q4 shipment slip.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO announcement day moved -9.5% (2026-08-26). That was not a print day.

outside_window.finding: Lead-plaintiff motion deadline in the securities class action (N.D. Cal.).

Actual shipment of the two Q4 annealing systems (FAU and one other) and delivery of the 17-qubit dual-rail gate-model system, both promised by year-end. The guidance on them resolves at the print (filed above); the physical events resolve later.
